newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends unchanged, off 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends unchanged, off 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to off 1/8 on the day in light activity.
Dollar bonds were off 1/8 and high grades off slightly, mostly in spots in the intermediate range and long end, traders said.
Overall activity was light to moderate in the morning and light in afternoon.

In an unusual move for the week, Lehman Brothers brought to market the largest issue of the week on a Friday. The firm priced and repriced a $943 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey deal.
The top yield in 2025 was lowered to 6.10 percent from 6.14 percent.

"It seems like they had it all institutionally done before they ever showed the Street," one trader said. "It didn't allow for anybody else to make money but the managers. So it's a little tough, but everybody's in that position any more. If they've got it, the want to keep it for themselves."
Municipal bond sales for the week of April 28 are expected to total $2.4 billion in 88 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $2 billion in 37 sales, with a $640 million NYC Municipal Water Agency deal through J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 51 sales totaling $453 million are on the schedule. A $115 million Montgomery County, Md., deal on Tuesday is the largest.
An additional 11 sales totaling $570 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds next week , depending on market conditions.
In the U.S. government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 5/32 at 93-20/32 to yield 7.14 percent.
In debt futures the June Municipal contract at the close was 112-7/32. The June T-bond contract was 107-4/32.
The MOB spread was 163 ticks, up from Thursday's close of 160 ticks.
